title: What does XLS-77 specify for Deep freeze?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XLS-77 and its practical limits.
body:
According to XLS specifications, XLS-77 adds deep-freeze controls for issued tokens, extending the restrictions available to an eligible issuer. [1]

The standard distinguishes deep freeze from ordinary freeze and account-wide options. The affected line's state and the issuer's permissions determine the supported operation. Do not infer that ordinary freeze, clawback and deep freeze have interchangeable effects. Holders should assess which controls apply to their exact asset and network before treating a balance as freely transferable. [1]

A published XLS document describes a design and its constraints; it is not by itself evidence that every network has enabled the corresponding amendment. Read the proposal status, dependencies and current network configuration together. Mainnet, Testnet and development networks can differ, and later fixes can change operational behavior. The source for XLS-77 was fetched directly from the public standards repository. [1][2]

The fetched specification records its status as Final. [1] Author interpretation: use XLS-77 as a specification reference and verify the actual network capability before promising it to a customer. Keep documented design, local tests and validated transactions separate when describing evidence. This article explains the standard rather than claiming a new live deployment. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
